title: BoJ Tankan (September 2026 survey) — released 08:50 JST, the same minute as that morning's Summary of Opinions
source: EST: boj.or.jp/en/statistics/outline/tkohyos.xlsx ('Schedule for Releases of Statistical Data (From July 2026 to June 2027)', linked from boj.or.jp/en/statistics/outline/ under 'Schedule for Releases of Statistical Data'), fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 48,500 bytes) and parsed cell-by-cell out of its 'Statistics data' sheet by this session. Row 230 reads 'Tankan (Short-Term Economic Survey of Enterprises in Japan) / Summary and Outline | 8:50 a.m. | ... | (Sept. Survey) | ...' and row 231 gives that column's date as Excel serial 46296 = 2026-10-01; the same row's June-survey cell is serial 46204 = 2026-07-01, which matches the June 2026 survey's ALREADY-PUBLISHED release date on boj.or.jp/en/statistics/tk/ ('July 1, 2026 | June 2026 Survey'), so the serial decoding is validated against an observed release rather than assumed. Release time corroborated verbatim from the Bank's own methodology page boj.or.jp/en/statistics/outline/exp/tk/extk.htm (HTTP 200, 66,232 bytes): 'The survey results are released at the beginning of April, July, October, and mid-December in principle (released at 8:50 a.m. Japan Standard Time). The release dates for the next one year are announced in advance at the end of June and December.' Cross-checked against the Bank's own TANKAN (Summary) archives (boj.or.jp/en/statistics/tk/gaiyo/{2011,2016,2021,2026}/index.htm, HTTP 200 each, 62 release dates parsed): every September survey since 2011 has published on the FIRST BUSINESS DAY OF OCTOBER, 15/15 (2011-10-03, 2012-10-01, 2013-10-01, 2014-10-01, 2015-10-01, 2016-10-03, 2017-10-02, 2018-10-01, 2019-10-01, 2020-10-01, 2021-10-01, 2022-10-03, 2023-10-02, 2024-10-01, 2025-10-01), and JPX's own market calendar (jpx.co.jp/english/corporate/about-jpx/calendar/, HTTP 200, 33,103 bytes, parsed today) lists Oct. 12 (Sports Day) as October 2026's ONLY closure, making Thursday 2026-10-01 the first business day of the month. Filed estimate on two counts, identical to the twelve BoJ entries already on this calendar: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has FED: for the Federal Reserve and no slot for the Bank of Japan, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep.
notes: DISCOVERED during the boj-summary-of-opinions-2026-10-01 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05), and filed because it destroys that ledger's inherited assumption rather than merely sitting near it. Four sibling Summary-of-Opinions ledgers concluded that the Tokyo cash bar is the ONE clean bar a BoJ meeting account owns — 08:50 JST is ten minutes before the 09:00 JST open, and Tokyo closes 15:30 JST, hours before any US print. boj-summary-of-opinions-2026-11-10 wrote that as an instruction: 'if a number is wanted, take Tokyo's.' At THIS venue that escape hatch does not exist: the Bank of Japan publishes the September Tankan and the September-MPM Summary of Opinions on the same date, at the same minute, into the same ten-minute pre-open window, and the Tankan is by any measure the larger release — a quarterly survey of ~10,000 enterprises drawn from a ~210,000-firm population under the Statistics Law, against a 1,391-word anonymised digest of an already-reported meeting. The collision is EXCLUSIVE to the September cohort: across all 86 Summaries of Opinions published 2016-2026, exactly 4 shared a date with a Tankan release (2021-10-01, 2022-10-03, 2023-10-02, 2024-10-01) and all four are accounts of a September MPM; the other seven meeting-month cohorts sit a minimum of 2-43 days from the nearest Tankan and have never collided. 2026 is the fifth such collision. Impact is MEDIUM rather than LOW — one tier above every BoJ meeting-account entry on this calendar — because unlike an anonymised opinion digest the Tankan is a first-release statistical print with a genuine surprise component and a documented Tokyo reaction function; it is not raised above MEDIUM because symbols is empty, no house playbook is rates- or FX-keyed, and the channel to this calendar's AI names runs through yen funding and global term premium, both second-order and both already owned by the FOMC ledgers. The 10-01 US session is separately owned and separately crowded: ism-manufacturing-2026-10-01 (high, CONFIRMED, 10:00 ET), with government-funding-deadline-2026-09-30 (high) and pce-2026-09-30 (high, CONFIRMED) the prior day and jobs-2026-10-02 (high, CONFIRMED) the next, so nothing in that tape is attributable to Tokyo without ruling those out first. One tape-history note for whoever scores this: the Nikkei has NO bar at all on 2020-10-01, that year's September-Tankan release date, because the Tokyo Stock Exchange halted trading for the entire session — so the cohort's Tankan-day sample is 9 sessions from 10 dates. Precedent for filing a non-MPM Bank of Japan statistical release as its own entry: japan-cpi-2026-12-18, kind 'macro-print'.
